he goes from that residence to another residence.
There too, the bhikkhus think thus:
“Friends, this bhikkhu has been subjected by the Saṅgha to a procedure of censure that is a semblance of the Dhamma by a unanimous assembly.
Come now, let us carry out a procedure of censure against him.
And they carried out a procedure of censure against him.
A faction acts contrary to the Dhamma.
He goes from that residence to another residence.
There too, the monks think:
‘Friends, this bhikkhu has been subjected by the Saṅgha to a censure transaction that is contrary to the Dhamma and carried out by a faction.
Come now, let us carry out a censure transaction against him.
And they carry out a censure transaction against him.
Being united but acting contrary to the Dhamma,
he goes from that residence to another residence.
There too, the monks think thus:
‘Friends, this bhikkhu has been subjected by the Saṅgha to a procedure of condemnation that was contrary to the Dhamma, though the Saṅgha was unanimous.
Come now, let us carry out a procedure of condemnation against him.
And they carried out a procedure of condemnation against him.
A faction acting according to the Dhamma goes from that residence to another residence.
There too, the monks think:
‘Friends, this bhikkhu has indeed been subjected by the Saṅgha to a procedure of censure that is legal and carried out by a faction.
Come now, let us carry out a procedure of censure against him.
And they carry out a procedure of censure against him.
By means of a counterfeit Dhamma, they form a faction.
10. Discussion on the Act of Subordination.
Here, monks, a monk is foolish, incompetent, prone to offenses, and lacking in restraint; he dwells in association with householders through improper associations with householders.
In that case, if the thought occurs to the monks:
“Friends, this monk is ignorant, incompetent, frequently committing offenses, and lacking in restraint; he dwells in association with householders in improper ways.
Come now, let us carry out a formal act of demotion against him,” then they should do so.
They perform a *niyassakamma* against him—
unlawfully and with an incomplete assembly.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
There too, the monks think:
“Friends, this monk has been subjected by the Saṅgha to a procedure of subordination that is contrary to the Dhamma and carried out by a faction.
Come now, let us subject him to a procedure of subordination.”
They perform a *niyassakamma* against him:
by an illegal procedure with a unanimous assembly … [and] by a legal procedure with a divided assembly …
A faction [acting] by means of a semblance of the Dhamma;
a united assembly [acting] by means of a semblance of the Dhamma...
[and so on]. As above, so should the wheel be constructed.
11. Discussion on the Act of Banishment.
Furthermore, monks, here a monk is a corrupter of families and of evil conduct.
If, in that case, the thought occurs to the monks:
‘Friends, this bhikkhu is a corrupter of families and of evil conduct.
Come now, let us carry out a formal act of banishment against him.
And they carried out a formal act of banishment against him.
A faction acts contrary to the Dhamma.
He goes from that residence to another residence.
There too, the monks think thus:
‘Friends, this bhikkhu has indeed been subjected by the Saṅgha to a procedure of banishment that is contrary to the Dhamma and carried out by a faction.
Come now, let us carry out a procedure of banishment against him.
And they carry out a procedure of banishment against him.
...in an illegal manner with a unanimous assembly;
...in a legal manner with a divided assembly;
...in a semblance of the Dhamma with a divided assembly; ...
[They act] with a semblance of Dhamma while being in concord… [as before]… A *cakka* (circle/diagram) should be drawn. 12.
Discussion on the Act of Reconciliation (*paṭisāraṇīyakamma*).
But here, monks, a monk reviles and abuses a householder.
If, in that situation, it occurs to the monks:
"Friends, this monk is reviling and abusing a householder."
"Let us perform a *paṭisāraṇīyakamma* against him.
They then perform a *paṭisāraṇīyakamma* against him in an illegitimate manner and by a faction.
So he goes from that residence to another residence.
There too, the monks think:
“Friends, this monk has been subjected by the Saṅgha to a procedure of reconciliation that is contrary to the Dhamma and carried out by an incomplete assembly.”
‘We shall carry out a procedure of reconciliation against him.
They carry out that procedure of reconciliation against him—unlawfully, but with a unanimous assembly... [and so on]...
A factional assembly that acts according to the Dhamma... a factional assembly that acts in a semblance of the Dhamma...
a united assembly that acts in a semblance of the Dhamma... [and so forth].
The wheel should be turned.
13. Discussion on the Act of Suspension for Refusal to See an Offense:
Now, monks, there is a monk who, having committed an offense, does not wish to see that offense.
In that case, if the thought occurs to the monks:
"Friends, this monk, having committed an offense, does not wish to see the offense.
Come now, let us carry out a formal act of suspension against him for failure to recognize an offense."
They carry out a formal act of suspension against him for not seeing an offense—
unrighteously and with a factional assembly.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
There too, the monks think:
“Friends, this monk has had a procedure of suspension for not seeing an offense carried out against him by a faction of the Saṅgha in an illegitimate manner.
Come now, let us carry out a procedure of suspension for not seeing an offense against him.”
They perform an act of suspension against him for not seeing an offense—
unlawfully, with a unanimous assembly … [and] lawfully, with a divided assembly …
A faction [acts] by means of a semblance of Dhamma … a united assembly [acts] by means of a semblance of Dhamma … [and so on].
A wheel should be turned.

14. Discussion on the Formal Act of Suspension for Refusal to Make Amends Furthermore, monks, there is the case where a monk, having committed an offense, does not wish to make amends for that offense.
If the thought occurs to the monks there:
‘Friends, this bhikkhu, having committed an offense, does not wish to make amends for that offense.
Come now, let us carry out a formal act of suspension against him for his failure to make amends for the offense.
And they carry out a formal act of suspension against him for his failure to make amends for the offense.
A faction acts contrary to the Dhamma.
He goes from that residence to another residence.
There too, the monks think:
‘Friends, this monk has been subjected by the Saṅgha to a procedure of suspension for not making amends for an offense, by an illegal act and by a faction.
Come now, let us carry out a procedure of suspension against him for not making amends for an offense.
And they carry out a procedure of suspension against him for not making amends for an offense.
...by an illegal procedure with a unanimous assembly;
...by a legal procedure with a divided assembly; ...by a semblance of a legal procedure with a divided assembly; ...
[They act] in a manner resembling the Dhamma while being in concord... [as before].
A *cakra* (diagram/table) should be drawn. 15. Discussion on the Act of Suspension for Non-Relinquishment.
"Furthermore, monks, here a monk does not wish to relinquish an evil view.
If, in that case, the monks think:
‘Friends, this monk does not wish to relinquish an evil view.’"
‘We shall carry out a procedure of suspension against Haṇḍa for not relinquishing an evil view.
They then carry out a procedure of suspension against him for not relinquishing that evil view—
unrighteously and with a faction.
So he goes from that residence to another residence.
There too, the monks think:
"Friends, this monk has been subjected by the Saṅgha to a procedure of suspension for not relinquishing an evil view, by means of an illegitimate act performed by an incomplete assembly."
“Let us carry out a formal act of suspension against Haṇḍa for not relinquishing his evil view.
They then carry out a formal act of suspension against him for not relinquishing his evil view—unrighteously, yet with a unanimous assembly. …pe…
A factional assembly that acts according to the Dhamma... a factional assembly that acts in a semblance of the Dhamma...
a united assembly that acts in a semblance of the Dhamma... [and so forth].
The wheel should be made.
16. Discussion on the Suspension of a Procedure of Censure.

Furthermore, monks, suppose a monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to a procedure of censure conducts himself properly, lowers his hair (in humility), behaves so as to deserve release, and requests the suspension of that procedure of censure.
In that case, if the thought occurs to the monks:

"Friends, this monk has been subjected to a procedure of censure by the Saṅgha; he is conducting himself properly, he is acting in accordance with the rules, he is striving for deliverance, and he requests the lifting of the censure procedure.
Come now, let us lift the censure procedure for him."
They rescind that act of censure against him—
being a faction acting contrary to the Dhamma.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks thought:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by the Saṅgha through an illegal procedure and with an incomplete assembly.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They rescind that act of censure against him by means of an illegal procedure while being unanimous.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks thought:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by the Saṅgha through an illegal procedure while they were in concord.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They rescind that act of censure against him by means of a legal procedure but with an incomplete assembly.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon the monks thought:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by the Saṅgha through a factional procedure that is in accordance with the Dhamma.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They rescind that act of censure in a manner that is a semblance of Dhamma, being a factional group.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
In that regard, the monks think:
“Friends, this monk’s act of condemnation has been lifted by a faction of the Saṅgha through a semblance of Dhamma.
Come now, let us lift his act of condemnation.”
They lift that censure transaction against him in a manner that is a semblance of Dhamma, yet they are united. But here, monks,

a monk who has had a censure transaction performed against him by the Saṅgha conducts himself properly, lowers his hair, behaves so as to deserve release, and asks for the lifting of the censure transaction.
In that case, if the thought occurs to the monks:

“Friends, this monk has been subjected to a censure transaction by the Saṅgha; he is conducting himself properly, he is acting in accordance with the requirements, he is behaving so as to deserve release, and he asks for the lifting of the censure transaction.
Come now, let us lift the censure transaction against him.”
They rescind that act of censure against him by an illegitimate procedure while being unanimous.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks think:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by the Saṅgha through an illegitimate procedure while they are in concord.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They rescind that act of censure against him—
being a faction acting contrary to the Dhamma.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks thought:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by the Saṅgha through a factional procedure that is in accordance with the Dhamma.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They rescind that act of censure in a manner that is a semblance of Dhamma, being a factional assembly.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
There, too, the monks think:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by a faction using a semblance of Dhamma.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They suspend that act of censure in a manner that is a semblance of Dhamma while being in concord.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks think:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by a united Saṅgha through a procedure that is a semblance of the Dhamma.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They suspend that act of censure:
being incomplete and contrary to the Dhamma.

But here, monks, a monk who has had an act of censure performed against him by the Saṅgha conducts himself properly, behaves in accordance with the Saṅgha’s expectations, and acts in a way that leads to his release; he asks for the suspension of the act of censure.
In that case, if the thought occurs to the monks:

"Friends, this monk has been subjected to a censure transaction by the Saṅgha; he is conducting himself properly, he is acting in accordance with the rules, he is behaving so as to deserve release, and he requests the lifting of the censure transaction.
Come now, let us lift the censure transaction for him."
They rescind that act of censure against him—
being a faction acting according to the Dhamma.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks thought:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by the Saṅgha through a factional procedure that is in accordance with the Dhamma.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They rescind that act of censure in a manner that is a semblance of Dhamma and with a factional assembly.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks think:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by a faction of the Saṅgha through a semblance of Dhamma.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They rescind that act of censure in a manner that is a semblance of Dhamma while being united.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the bhikkhus thought:
“Friends, this bhikkhu’s act of censure has been lifted by a unanimous Saṅgha through a procedure that is a semblance of the Dhamma.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They rescind that act of censure against him by means of an illegal procedure and a factional assembly.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks thought:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by the Saṅgha through an illegal procedure and with an incomplete assembly.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They suspend that act of censure by means of an illegitimate procedure while being unanimous. But here, monks,

a monk who has been subjected to an act of censure by the Saṅgha conducts himself properly, behaves in accordance with the rules, acts so as to deserve release, and requests the suspension of the act of censure.
In that case, if the thought occurs to the monks:

“Friends, this monk has been subjected by the Saṅgha to a censure transaction; he is conducting himself properly, he is acting in accordance with the requirements, he is not acting contrary to them, and he asks for the lifting of the censure transaction.
Come now, let us lift the censure transaction for him.”
They rescind that act of censure in a manner that is a semblance of Dhamma, being a faction.
He goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks thought:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by a faction of the Saṅgha through a semblance of Dhamma.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They rescind that act of censure against him—
a semblance of Dhamma, performed by a unanimous assembly.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks thought:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by a unanimous Saṅgha through a semblance of Dhamma.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They rescind that act of censure against him—
being a faction acting contrary to the Dhamma.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks thought:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by the Saṅgha through an illegitimate procedure by a faction.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They rescind that act of censure against him by an illegitimate procedure while being unanimous.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks thought:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by the Saṅgha through an illegitimate procedure while they were in concord.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They suspend that act of censure:
a faction acting according to the Dhamma.

Now, monks, suppose a monk against whom an act of censure has been carried out by the Saṅgha conducts himself properly, lowers his pride, behaves in a way that leads to his release, and asks for the suspension of the act of censure.
In that case, if the thought occurs to the monks:

"Friends, this monk has been subjected to a procedure of censure by the Saṅgha; he is conducting himself properly, he is acting in accordance with the spirit of the law, he is striving for deliverance, and he asks for the suspension of the censure procedure.
Come now, let us suspend the censure procedure against him."
They rescind that censure transaction against him—
being united, but in a manner that is a semblance of Dhamma.
He goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks thought:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by a united Saṅgha through a semblance of Dhamma.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They rescind that act of censure against him by an illegal procedure and with an incomplete assembly.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks thought:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by the Saṅgha through an illegitimate procedure by a faction.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They rescind that act of censure against him by an illegitimate procedure while being unanimous.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks thought:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by the Saṅgha through an illegitimate procedure while they were in concord.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They rescind that act of censure against him by means of a factional procedure that is contrary to the Dhamma.
He then goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks thought:
“Friends, this monk’s act of censure has been lifted by the Saṅgha through a factional procedure that is in accordance with the Dhamma.
Come now, let us lift his act of censure.”
They resolve that censure transaction for him—being a faction acting in a manner that merely resembles the Dhamma. 17.
Discussion on the Resolution of the Transaction of Demotion.

"Furthermore, monks, here a monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to the act of demotion conducts himself properly, behaves in accordance with the requirements, acts toward his own deliverance, and requests the lifting of that act of demotion.
If, in this case, the monks think:

'Friends, this monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to the act of demotion conducts himself properly, behaves in accordance with the requirements, acts toward his own deliverance, and requests the lifting of that act of demotion.'"
‘We shall revoke the act of demotion against this monk. They revoke his act of demotion—
being a faction acting contrary to the Dhamma.
So he goes from that residence to another residence.
There too, the monks think:
“Friends, this monk’s act of demotion has been revoked by the Saṅgha through an illegal procedure by a faction.”
‘We shall revoke the act of demotion against this monk.
They revoke his act of demotion—unlawfully, yet with a unanimous assembly... [and so on]...
A factional assembly that acts according to the Dhamma... a factional assembly that acts according to a semblance of the Dhamma...
a united assembly that acts according to a semblance of the Dhamma... [and so forth].
The wheel should be turned.
18. Discussion on the Lifting of the Act of Banishment:

Now, monks, suppose a monk against whom an act of banishment has been carried out by the Saṅgha conducts himself properly, lowers his hair (in humility), behaves so as to deserve release, and requests the lifting of that act of banishment.
In that case, if the thought occurs to the monks:

“Friends, this monk has been subjected by the Saṅgha to a formal act of banishment; he is conducting himself properly, he is acting in accordance with the Saṅgha’s wishes, he is striving for his release, and he requests the lifting of the formal act of banishment.
Come now, let us lift the formal act of banishment for him.”
They rescind that act of banishment—
being a faction acting contrary to the Dhamma.
He goes from that residence to another residence.
Thereupon, the monks thought:
“Friends, this monk’s act of banishment has been rescinded by the Saṅgha through an illegitimate procedure by a faction.
Come now, let us rescind his act of banishment.”
They rescind that act of banishment:
by an illegitimate procedure with a unanimous assembly...
[or] by a legitimate procedure with a divided assembly...
[A formal act] by a faction with what is a semblance of the Dhamma … [a formal act] by a united assembly with what is a semblance of the Dhamma … [and so on].
A wheel should be drawn.

19. Discussion on the Cessation of the Act of Reconciliation In this case, monks, a monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to the act of reconciliation conducts himself properly, behaves in accordance with the Saṅgha’s wishes, and acts in a way that leads to his release; he then requests the cessation of the act of reconciliation.
If, in that situation, it occurs to the monks:

‘Friends, this monk has been subjected to a *paṭisāraṇīya* (reconciliation) legal procedure by the Saṅgha; he is conducting himself properly, he is acting in accordance with the community, he is behaving so as not to cause further trouble, and he asks for the lifting of the *paṭisāraṇīya* procedure.
Let us, then, lift the *paṭisāraṇīya* procedure against him.
They then lift the *paṭisāraṇīya* procedure against him.
A faction acts contrary to the Dhamma.
He goes from that residence to another residence.
There too, the bhikkhus think thus:
‘Friends, this bhikkhu’s act of reconciliation has been lifted by the Saṅgha through an illegitimate procedure by a faction.
Come now, let us lift his act of reconciliation. They then lift his act of reconciliation.
... by an illegal procedure with a unanimous assembly ...
by a legal procedure with a divided assembly ... by a semblance of a legal procedure with a divided assembly ...
[The Saṅgha] being in concord [but acting] by means of a semblance of the Dhamma … [as before] … A wheel should be drawn. 20.
Discussion on the Cessation of the Act of Suspension for Non-Confession.
But here, monks, a monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to a formal act of suspension for not seeing an offense conducts himself properly,
lowers his hair (in submission), behaves so as to deserve release, and asks for the rescission of the formal act of suspension for not seeing an offense.
In that case, if the thought occurs to the monks:
“Friends, this monk has been subjected by the Saṅgha to a procedure of suspension for not seeing an offense;

he is conducting himself properly, he is acting in accordance with the rules, he is behaving so as to deserve release, and he asks for the revocation of the procedure of suspension for not seeing an offense.”
‘We shall rescind the act of suspension for not seeing an offense against Handa.
They rescind the act of suspension for not seeing an offense against him while being a faction acting contrary to the Dhamma.
So he goes from that residence to another residence.
There too, the monks think:
“Friends, this monk’s act of suspension for not seeing an offense has been lifted by the Saṅgha through an illegitimate procedure and by a faction.”
‘We shall rescind the act of suspension for not seeing an offense against Haṇḍa.
They rescind the act of suspension for not seeing an offense against him—unlawfully, but with a unanimous assembly. …pe…
A faction acting according to the Dhamma...
a faction acting in a semblance of the Dhamma...
a united assembly acting in a semblance of the Dhamma... [and so forth].
The wheel (of the formal act) should be performed.
21. Discussion on the Subsidence of the Act of Suspension for Non-Expiation of an Offense:
Now, monks, suppose a monk has been subjected by the Saṅgha to the formal act of suspension for non-expiation of an offense.
He conducts himself properly, he shows respect, he acts in such a way as to deserve release, and he asks for the lifting of the suspension procedure imposed for his failure to atone for an offense.
If, in that case, the monks think thus:
"Friends, this bhikkhu has been subjected by the Saṅgha to a formal act of suspension for not making amends for an offense;

yet he conducts himself properly, behaves with humility, and acts in a way that leads to his release. He now requests the lifting of the formal act of suspension for not making amends for the offense."
‘We shall rescind the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense against Haṇḍa.
They rescind the act of suspension for not making amends for that offense while being a faction acting contrary to the Dhamma.
So he goes from that residence to another residence.
There too, the monks think:
"Friends, this monk’s act of suspension for not making amends for an offense has been lifted by the Saṅgha."
‘Let us, by means of an illegal procedure and with a faction, suspend his act of suspension for not making amends for an offense.
They then suspend his act of suspension for not making amends for an offense.
... by an illegal procedure with a unanimous assembly;
... by a legal procedure with a divided assembly; ... by a semblance of the Dhamma with a divided assembly; ...
... [the Saṅgha] is united by means of a semblance of the Dhamma ... [and so on].
A *cakra* (wheel) should be made.
22. Discussion on the Suspension of the Act of Suspension for Non-Relinquishment.

But here, monks, a monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to a formal act of suspension for not relinquishing an evil view conducts himself properly, lowers his hair (in submission), behaves so as to deserve release,
and requests the lifting of the formal act of suspension for not relinquishing an evil view.
In that case, if it occurs to the monks:
“Friends, this monk has been subjected by the Saṅgha to a formal act of suspension for not relinquishing an evil view;
yet he conducts himself properly, lowers his hair (submits), and behaves in a way that leads to his release from that non-relinquishment of an evil view.”
He requests the lifting of the *ukkhepanīyakamma* (act of suspension).
“Come now, let us lift this act of suspension for not relinquishing an evil view.
They then lift that act of suspension for not relinquishing an evil view.
A faction acts contrary to the Dhamma.
He goes from that residence to another residence.
There too, the monks think thus:
"Friends, the Sangha has lifted this monk’s procedure of suspension for not relinquishing an evil view—
unlawfully and by a faction.
Come, let us lift his procedure of suspension for not relinquishing an evil view."
They suspend the act of suspension against him for not relinquishing that evil view:
by an illegal procedure with a unanimous assembly … [and] by a legal procedure with a divided assembly …
[A formal act] by a faction with what resembles the Dhamma;
[a formal act] by a united assembly with what resembles the Dhamma...
[and so on]. A wheel should be made.
23. Discussion on the Dispute Concerning the Act of Censure.
Furthermore, monks, there is a monk here who is a maker of strife, a maker of quarrels, a maker of disputes, a maker of contention, and a creator of legal issues within the Saṅgha.
In that case, if it occurs to the monks thus:
‘Friends, this bhikkhu is a quarrelsome one...
[as before] ...a creator of legal issues in the Saṅgha.
Come now, let us carry out a censure transaction against him.’”
They perform that act of censure against him—
illegitimately and with a faction.
While staying there, the Saṅgha disputes.
‘An illegal procedure by a divided assembly; an illegal procedure by a united assembly; a legal procedure by a divided assembly; a semblance of a legal procedure by a divided assembly;
a semblance of a legal procedure by a united assembly; an unperformed act; a badly performed act; an act that must be done again.
In this regard, monks, those monks who speak thus—
‘An illegal factional transaction’: those monks who say, “This transaction is not done;
it is a badly done transaction; the transaction must be done again”—these monks there are speakers of Dhamma.
But here, monks, a monk is a maker of strife … [as before] …”
There is a monk who causes legal disputes in the Saṅgha.
And if it occurs to the monks there:
“Friends, this monk is one who creates quarrels... [as before]...”
“He is a creator of legal disputes in the Saṅgha.
Let us perform a censure transaction against him.
So they performed a censure transaction against him.
In accordance with what is not Dhamma, they are united.
While staying there, the Saṅgha disputes:
“A factional act contrary to the Dhamma; a united act contrary to the Dhamma; a factional act in accordance with the Dhamma; an act that is a semblance of the Dhamma...”
"A factional legal act; a united legal act that is a semblance of Dhamma; an unperformed legal act; a wrongly performed legal act; a legal act that must be performed again.
In this regard, monks, as for those monks who say, "It is an illegal united legal act," and those monks who say:
‘An act that has not been performed, an improperly performed act, must be performed again as a formal act’—these are the monks who speak according to the Dhamma in that matter.
But here, monks, a monk is a maker of strife...
[as before] ...a maker of legal disputes in the Saṅgha.
In that case, if the monks think:
“Friends, this monk is a maker of quarrels... a maker of legal issues in the Saṅgha; come now, let us carry out a censure transaction against him,” they carry out a censure transaction against him.
A factional legal act.
While staying there, the Saṅgha disputes:

“It was a factional act contrary to the Dhamma; it was a united act contrary to the Dhamma; it was a factional act in accordance with the Dhamma; it was a semblance of a legal act in accordance with the Dhamma.”
"A factional legal act; a united legal act that is a semblance of Dhamma; an unperformed legal act; a poorly performed legal act; a legal act that must be performed again.
